g.data-label: D4 · why routing is all-or-nothing within a profile the pinned runtime supplies no virtual clock, so there is no interval in which a residual direct std/clock.now read is merely unrecorded-but-deterministic — such a read is nondeterministic, and is a hermeticity failure like any other unrouted ambient effect, caught by D5's mechanisms rather than a clock-specific one a profile may be narrow, but within its declared scope the clock seam is total

g.data-label: 'profile-reachable' is installation-scoped, not a reachability analysis a site or hook is profile-reachable when it is 1 · in the core driver, or 2 · in a module the profile installs, or 3 · in a core code path guarded solely by an installed hook's identity all three are answered by the extension list plus the module inventory, both enumerable today · the term covers effect sites and hooks alike: a profile-reachable hook is every hook the profile installs, run or not it does not mean 'a site some execution path can actually perform' — deciding that needs the analysis obligation 3 declines to require and nothing here builds · the consequence is deliberately conservative: a site in an installed extension must be routed even if no corpus run reaches it clause 3 is not a technicality — without it, runtime.ail:190 is either always reachable, making the driver's obligation five sites, or unclassified

tspan.tspan: 'profile-reachable' is installation-scoped, not a reachability analysis

g.data-label: the detection set is enumerated, versioned, and derived from the toolchain the classifier is the pinned toolchain's effect-bearing stdlib and builtin surface, as module plus exported symbol, from ailang builtins list --by-effect, constrained by the profile's permitted capabilities the two available enumerations disagree — 18 effect labels in the v0.26.0 builtin surface against 12 permitted by ailang.toml — so neither alone is a classifier and a hand-maintained list would silently rot re-deriving it is a required step of every toolchain repin, and the derived set is recorded with the profile or manifest match on the imported target module, not on bound symbol names: aliased and qualified forms typecheck on the pin, so a name-matching inventory would miss them by construction · nothing at HEAD aliases std/clock, which is why this has cost nothing so far and exactly why it must be specified rather than assumed effects reached through an ExtPorts or Ports closure are covered — the closure is written literally at a site inside its defining module, and what the scan cannot follow is the call edge, which an ambient inventory does not need

g.data-label: withholding the Clock capability is a coarse run-time backstop an earlier revision called it 'a build-and-profile-level gate, not an in-execution one'. It is neither. Clock stays in the effect row and AILANG fails only when a read is actually performed: a function whose row contains Clock but whose taken branch never calls now() runs to completion with it withheld verified against the real driver — the deterministic entry point completes with Clock withheld while the live world on the same driver dies the correction cuts both ways: stronger than assumed, because it catches unrouted reads on paths a run actually takes; weaker, because it says nothing about reachable paths a run did not exercise, so it cannot on its own discharge the all-or-nothing rule · the source and ABI audit remains the primary detector
